hints: A subarray XOR is the XOR of two distinct prefix positions.
Count pairs of prefix XOR values using XOR convolution.
The Walsh-Hadamard transform computes all XOR-convolution coefficients together.
analogy: Pair every prefix with every other prefix at once; XOR convolution groups these pairs by their XOR.
example: For [1,1], prefix XORs are [0,1,0]; possible nonempty subarray XORs are 0 and 1.
algorithm: Build frequencies of the n+1 prefix XORs, including zero. Apply the XOR Walsh-Hadamard transform, square every transformed coefficient, and apply the inverse transform. For x>0 include x if its coefficient is positive; for x=0 include it if its coefficient exceeds n+1, since the diagonal pairs use identical positions. Print included values in increasing order. Use wide integer arithmetic.
correctness: The XOR convolution coefficient for x counts ordered pairs of prefix positions whose XOR is x. For nonzero x these positions are automatically distinct; for zero, subtracting the n+1 diagonal pairs leaves exactly pairs corresponding to nonempty subarrays.
complexity: For n values and universe size U=2^20, O(n+U log U) time and O(U) space.
